mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES continues to recover while TRANSIT remains less negative, commuting-linked foot traffic should keep pulling RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks because more workers pass through commercial areas before and after work.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise relative to the last 28 days even though WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both become less negative for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A continued rise in GROCERY_PHARM indicates households are already increasing essential trips, which spills into nearby discretionary shopping and pushes RETAIL_REC higher within one to two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays flat or falls over the next 14 days while GROCERY_PHARM remains above its prior weekly mean.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS mobility stops improving and remains deeply negative, outdoor leisure substitution weakens and retail outings keep recovering; this should lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS stays below -30 for at least 2 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to improve over the next 28 days while PARKS remains below -30 in weekly means.

mechanism_narrative: A renewed drop in TRANSIT together with a simultaneous rise in RESIDENTIAL implies tighter containment behavior, which should suppress discretionary shopping and reduce RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls at least 5 points week-on-week while RESIDENTIAL rises at least 1 point week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall in the next week after a joint TRANSIT drop and RESIDENTIAL rise of the stated size.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES remains elevated for two consecutive weeks after the current trough, the lagged effect of returning office activity should broaden lunch and after-work spending and raise RETAIL_REC over the following month.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises for 2 consecutive weeks from its current level
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is lower over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days despite a two-week rise in WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: A widening gap where RESIDENTIAL stays above baseline while TRANSIT stays below baseline means people are substituting home-based routines for outing-based consumption, so RETAIL_REC should remain depressed over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days while RESIDENTIAL stays above +8 and TRANSIT stays below -15.

mechanism_narrative: Under a stable seasonal pattern, persistent weakness in PARKS combined with only a mild recovery in GROCERY_PHARM means weekend discretionary trips are not yet broadening, so RETAIL_REC should still edge down over four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is higher over the next 28 days while PARKS remains very negative and GROCERY_PHARM does not accelerate further.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM loses momentum after its recent jump while TRANSIT also turns down, the retail rebound will lose support quickly and RETAIL_REC will fall within one week as trips consolidate back into essentials.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM declines from the prior week and TRANSIT also declines week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline in the next week after both GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT weaken.
